morph.note: Perfect of √वच् with samprasāraṇa in the reduplication (उ-वाच); the narrative past, as in 1.1.

mantras.anvaya_en: Subject and verb: a speaker label.

comm.t: The Devī answers the gods. At the end of chapter 11 she has granted them a boon and promised to return whenever demons oppress the world (11.37–55); now, still before them, she adds her own account of what the recitation of her deeds will bring. The speech runs to 12.30, after which Medhas resumes the narrative (12.31). In recitation this mantra carries the bīja ॐ, which belongs to the pāṭha, not to the verse.

Final m before a consonant is written as anusvāra; so also नित्यं स्तोष्यते, सकलां बाधां.
Final i before a dissimilar vowel becomes y.

samasa.alt: Also analysed as a nañ tatpuruṣa, न संशयः, whose accusative neuter is used as an adverb; the sense is the same.

morph.note: Simple future of √स्तु: guṇa of the root vowel (स्तो-) + स्य + ते. √स्तु takes both padas (स्तौति / स्तुते); the ātmanepada future is regular, and the verb is active: its object is माम्.
Future of the causative stem नाशय- (√नश् with vṛddhi + णिच्) + इष्य + मि: ‘I will cause to perish’.
Past participle of सम् + आ + √धा; धा is replaced by हि before क्त, giving -हित. ‘Put together’, hence ‘collected, concentrated’.

mantras.anvaya: यः समाहितः (सन्) एभिः स्तवैः च मां नित्यं स्तोष्यते, तस्य सकलां बाधाम् अहम् असंशयं नाशयिष्यामि।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative–correlative sentence: the relative clause (यः … स्तोष्यते) describes the devotee; the main clause, with अहम् as subject, gives the promise.
mantras.lit: And whoever, with a collected mind, will constantly praise me with these hymns — every affliction of his I will destroy, without doubt.
mantras.tr: Whoever praises me daily with these hymns, with a mind at rest in me, every trouble of his I will surely destroy.
mantras.tr_note: ‘With a mind at rest in me’ renders समाहितः, ‘collected, concentrated’; the object of the concentration is implied by the context.

comm.t: The first promise of the phalaśruti. ‘These hymns’ (एभिः स्तवैः) are the praises the gods have just sung — above all the hymn of chapter 11 — and, by extension, the other hymns of the text (chapters 1, 4 and 5). The condition is twofold: regularity (नित्यम्) and attention (समाहितः).
In the Śākta tradition this verse is cited to justify the daily recitation of the hymns of the Saptaśatī on their own, apart from the whole text, when time does not allow the full pāṭha.
A modern reading: the promise is made not to the learned but to the attentive. What the verse asks for is steadiness of mind, not ritual elaboration.

samasa.sense: the story of the first carita (chapter 1)

samasa.literal: the slaying of Mahiṣa the asura
samasa.sense: the story of the middle carita (chapters 2–4)
the two brothers of the last carita (chapters 5–10); dual because two are named

morph.note: घातन is an action noun (ल्युट्, -अन) from the causative of √हन्, whose causative stem is घातय-: ‘causing to be slain, slaughter’.
The taddhita affix वति (-vat) makes an indeclinable of likeness: तद्वत् ‘like that, in the same way’.
Future of a curādi root: the present stem कीर्तय- is kept and इष्य is added. The future in a relative clause states the condition of the promise to come.

mantras.anvaya: ये मधुकैटभनाशं च महिषासुरघातनं (च) तद्वत् शुम्भनिशुम्भयोः वधं (च) कीर्तयिष्यन्ति, …
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause with three objects, one for each carita; its correlative (तेषाम्) comes in 12.5, after a second relative clause in 12.4.
mantras.lit: Those who will proclaim the destruction of Madhu and Kaiṭabha and the slaying of the asura Mahiṣa, and likewise the killing of Śumbha and Niśumbha —
mantras.tr: Those who recite the destruction of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, the slaying of Mahiṣāsura, and likewise the killing of Śumbha and Niśumbha —

comm.t: The Devī names the three stories of the text in order: Madhu and Kaiṭabha (chapter 1), Mahiṣa (chapters 2–4), Śumbha and Niśumbha (chapters 5–10). What is to be recited is the whole narrative, not the hymns alone.

The verse is read as the Goddess’s own authority for the three-carita structure of the pāṭha. The Gita Press pāṭha assigns the three caritas to Mahākālī, Mahālakṣmī and Mahāsarasvatī as presiding forms; that is liturgical tradition, not stated here.

morph.note: Future of √श्रु: guṇa श्रो- + स्य + अन्ति, without the connecting इ (an aniṭ root). The present stem शृणु- plays no part in it.
Locative of time of a feminine ī-stem: -ई + आम् → -याम्. The feminine agrees with the unexpressed तिथि ‘lunar day’; likewise चतुर्दश्याम्, नवम्याम्.

mantras.anvaya: ये च एव अष्टम्यां चतुर्दश्यां नवम्यां च एकचेतसः (सन्तः) भक्त्या मम उत्तमं माहात्म्यं श्रोष्यन्ति, …
mantras.anvaya_en: A second relative clause, parallel to 12.3: the first speaks of those who recite, this one of those who listen. Both are taken up by तेषाम् in 12.5.
mantras.lit: And also those who, with one-pointed minds, on the eighth, the fourteenth and the ninth (lunar days), will listen with devotion to my supreme Māhātmya —
mantras.tr: and those who, on the eighth, the fourteenth and the ninth days of the lunar fortnight, listen with devotion and undivided mind to this supreme account of my glory —
mantras.tr_note: ‘Of the lunar fortnight’ makes explicit the तिथि implied by the feminine ordinals. ‘Account of my glory’ renders माहात्म्यम्, which here names the text.

comm.t: The Devī names three lunar days (tithis) as especially fit for hearing the text: the eighth, the fourteenth and the ninth. The verse speaks of listening, as 12.3 spoke of reciting; both are then promised the same fruit in 12.5.

Aṣṭamī and navamī, above all in the bright fortnight of the autumn month Āśvina, are the climactic days of the Navarātra worship of Durgā, and caturdaśī is traditionally sacred to the Goddess in her fierce forms. The tradition takes these as the days for the full pāṭha.

words.en: separation from those dear to them
words.g: n. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)

sandhi.note: Final t becomes d before the voiced d; written with a virāma and a space.
-āḥ before a voiced sound: the visarga (as रु) becomes y and is dropped, leaving -ā.
च + एव → चैव (a + e → ai); एव + इष्ट… → एवेष्ट… (a + i → e).

samasa.sense: an evil deed, sin; the s of दुस् becomes ṣ before k
misfortunes that are the fruit of past wrongdoing
samasa.alt: The final member उत्थ is a kṛt derivative of उद् + √स्था (‘rising up’), so the compound can also be classed as an upapada tatpuruṣa; the ablative relation is the same.

Also readable as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, इष्टानां वियोजनम् ‘the separation of the dear ones’. With वि + √युज् the person one is parted from is normally in the instrumental, so the tṛtīyā analysis fits better.

morph.note: Future of √भू (भव् + इष्य + ति). It is singular, agreeing with the nearest subject (दारिद्र्यम्), and is understood in every clause of the verse, including the plural आपदः (where भविष्यन्ति is meant).
Abstract noun from दरिद्र ‘poor’ by the taddhita affix ष्यञ् (-य) with vṛddhi of the first syllable: ‘the state of being poor’.
Nominative plural of the feminine consonant stem आपद् (आ + √पद्, ‘what befalls’).

mantras.anvaya: तेषां किञ्चित् दुष्कृतं न (भविष्यति), दुष्कृतोत्थाः आपदः च न (भविष्यन्ति), दारिद्र्यं न भविष्यति, इष्टवियोजनं च एव न (भविष्यति)।
mantras.anvaya_en: The main clause for the relatives of 12.3–4: four negated clauses share one verb, भविष्यति, with तेषाम् as the genitive of possession (‘for them there will be no …’).
mantras.lit: For them there will be no evil deed whatever, nor misfortunes arising from evil deeds; there will be no poverty, nor indeed separation from those dear to them.
mantras.tr: For them no sin will remain, nor the misfortunes that sin brings; they will know neither poverty nor parting from those they love.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Will remain’ renders the negated भविष्यति for दुष्कृतम्, where ‘there will be no sin for them’ would be stiff; the sense is that sin will not attach to them.

comm.t: The fruit promised to those of 12.3–4 is negative: four things will not befall them — sin (दुष्कृतम्), its consequences (दुष्कृतोत्थाः आपदः), poverty, and separation from the beloved. The order moves from the moral cause to its worldly results.
The pairing of दुष्कृत with दुष्कृतोत्थाः आपदः is read in the light of the doctrine of karma: the recitation is said to remove not only present misfortunes but their root in past deeds.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) names the Goddess पापनाशिनी (name 167) and सर्वापद्विनिवारिणी (name 913), ‘destroyer of sin’ and ‘warder-off of all misfortunes’: the same two promises as this verse, made in a separate work.
